# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P37](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0037)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Ruby is a fair and showy young lady with large, bright-blue eyes, a brilliant complexion, a plump figure, and long golden hair that she wears in braids. She was widely considered the handsomest girl of her year at Queen's Academy. Near the end of her life, she grew very thin and pale, with a hectic flush on her cheeks and hands that were almost transparent.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)_

## Personality

Ruby is cheerful, good-tempered, and frivolous, possessing a great love for laughter, pleasant social life, fancy work, and suitors. She lacks interest in deep intellectual topics or books, preferring frank enjoyment of lightweight amusements. Though prone to laughing and chattering, she can be easily frightened or nervous, as shown by her dread of play-acting or death. When faced with a fatal illness, she fought desperately to maintain a hopeful, gay mask to hide her terror.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c28 P13](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0013), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v3 c11 P10](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0010), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P14](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0014)_

## History

Ruby grew up in Avonlea as a schoolmate and playfellow of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews. During a summer outing by Orchard Slope pond, she joined her friends in dramatizing Tennyson's Elaine, though she declined to play the title role due to fear of lying down pretending to be dead. Later, she attended Queen's Academy alongside her Avonlea peers and was widely recognized as the handsomest girl in her year. During this period, Gilbert Blythe frequently accompanied her home on weekends and carried her satchel, though she found his intellectual conversations confusing compared to other suitors. After completing her studies, she took up teaching as a profession. However, she contracted galloping consumption during the winter, forcing her to step down from teaching while harboring hopes of securing the White Sands school in the fall. Throughout the following summer, she clung to a mask of giddiness and constantly talked about her suitors, while secretly struggling with the terrifying knowledge of her approaching end. One evening in the garden, she confessed her deep fear of dying and leaving her accustomed life to Anne. Shortly after, she passed away quietly in her sleep and was buried in a white velvet casket in the Avonlea graveyard.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v1 c35 P0](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0000), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c11 P7](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0007), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P31](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0031), [v3 c14 P36](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0036)_

## Quotes

> I don't mind floating down when there's two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It's fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn't. I'd die really of fright.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Anne, it won't be long now before I'll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I'll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)</sub>

> I don't want to die. I'm afraid to die.  <sub>[v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011)</sub>

> Because—because—oh, I'm not afraid but that I'll go to heaven, Anne. I'm a church member. But—it'll be all so different. I think—and think—and I get so frightened—and—and—homesick. Heaven must be very beautiful, of course, the Bible says so—but, Anne, it won't be what 've been used to.  <sub>[v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>
